# Namespace `qb::http` / `qb::http1` — HTTP/1.1 server, one-shot client, persistent client (`1.1/`)

### Server (plaintext) — `src/qbm/http/1.1/http.h`
- `qb::http::DefaultSession` — default non-SSL per-connection session.
- `template<typename Session=DefaultSession> class Server : public use<Server<Session>>::server<Session>` — HTTP/1.1 server; `Router<Session>& router()`; listen via inherited `internal::server::listen`. Alias `template<...> using server = Server<Session>`.
- `template<typename Session=DefaultSession> std::unique_ptr<Server<Session>> make_server();` — factory.
- `internal::server::drain(qb::duration deadline, std::function<void(qb::http::drain_outcome)> on_drained = {}) -> bool` (`http.h:1069`; Huly QB-167) -- closes the listening socket (a new connection is refused), closes each idle session gracefully (`DisconnectedReason::ServerDraining`, qb-io's lingering close), lets each busy one answer every request it has received -- the last answer `Connection: close` -- and runs `on_drained` once on the server's loop: `drained` when the last owned HTTP or in-place WebSocket session is gone (a lingering one counts), before drain() returns when none is open; `deadline` when `deadline` came first, after aborting what is open (`ServerDraining`); a deadline of zero or less aborts at once. A WebSocket upgraded in place and still owned by this server is sent `1001 Going Away` and is waited for until it closes or the deadline aborts it (Huly QB-1097). A session extracted for an upgrade belongs to its new owner and remains outside the drain (`extractSession`, `http.h:1121`); extraction may finish the old owner's drain. Returns false (and changes nothing) when a drain is already under way; the server cannot listen again. `draining() const noexcept` (`http.h:1098`). Session hooks: `http1_begin_drain()`, `http1_abort_drain()`, `http1_speaks_http()` (`http.h:598`, `:614`, `:585`); `qb::protocol::http::server::dispatching_size()` (`1.1/protocol/server.h:103`) tells a session whether another request follows the one being answered.
- `internal::server::listen(qb::io::uri uri, std::filesystem::path cert_file={}, std::filesystem::path key_file={}) -> bool` — bind/listen; **returns true == listening** (it returns `!transport().listen(...)`). Secure transport sets ALPN `{"http/1.1"}`.
- `internal::session::keep_alive(bool=true)`; `internal::session::max_pipelined_requests(std::size_t) noexcept` (default 128, exceed → disconnect `ByProtocolError`); `internal::session::context() -> std::shared_ptr<Context<Derived>>` (null when idle); `internal::session::send_response(ContextType&)`; `internal::io_handler::router() -> Router&`. `internal::session::stream_high_watermark() const noexcept` / `stream_high_watermark(std::size_t bytes) noexcept -> Derived&` (`http.h:772`, `:776`; Huly QB-86) — the high mark a stream begun on this session starts with (1 MiB). The session's destructor calls `cancel_live_stream()` (`http.h:564-566`): a server destroyed under a live stream sends no disconnected event, and the producer is told all the same.
- `struct qb::http::request_limits { std::size_t max_url_length, max_header_name_length, max_header_value_length, max_headers_count, max_chunk_size, max_body_size; constexpr request_limits normalized() const noexcept; }` (`1.1/protocol/base.h:97`) — the limits a server reads every request under, on every version (Huly QB-94); each defaults to its `protocol_limits` constant, 0 = none, and `normalized()` reads each 0 as the largest size. `max_headers_count` counts the regular fields of one section (the header section, then the trailer section on its own); `max_chunk_size` is HTTP/1.1's.
- `internal::io_handler::set_request_limits(qb::http::request_limits const&) noexcept` / `[[nodiscard]] qb::http::request_limits const& request_limits() const noexcept` (`http.h:882`, `:890`) — the limits every request is read under (Huly QB-94), same call as the HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and dual-stack servers'; read when each request begins, 0 = none, defaults the `protocol_limits` constants. A request over one is answered with `Connection: close` after every request received before it -- `414` for the target, `431` for a field name, a field value or a section's field count, `413` for a chunk or the body (a declared `Content-Length` at the end of the header section, a chunked body when it passes the limit) -- and the connection closes after that delivery (qb-io's lingering close); each closed with no answer until 3.3 (Huly QB-168, QB-94). `set_max_body_size(std::size_t) noexcept` / `[[nodiscard]] std::size_t max_body_size() const noexcept` (`http.h:903`, `:911`) set and read the body limit alone (the transport's input-buffer cap stays under 0). Protocol hooks, public because the protocol detects them with a `requires`-expression: `internal::session::http_request_limits()` (`http.h:655`), `internal::session::http1_refuse_request(qb::http::Status) noexcept` (`http.h:675`); `Parser<M>::set_request_limits(qb::http::request_limits const&)` / `request_limits()` / `set_max_body_size(std::size_t)` / `max_body_size()` / `refusal_status()` (`1.1/protocol/base.h:817`, `:825`, `:833`, `:841`, `:855`).
Usage: `auto s = qb::http::make_server(); s->router().get("/", h); s->router().compile(); s->listen(qb::io::uri{"tcp://0.0.0.0:8080"}); s->start();`

### Server (HTTPS) — `src/qbm/http/1.1/http.h` · **needs `QB_HAS_SSL`**
- `qb::http::ssl::DefaultSecureSession`; `template<typename Session=DefaultSecureSession> class ssl::Server` (`router()` const+non-const); `template<typename Session=DefaultSecureSession> std::unique_ptr<ssl::Server<Session>> ssl::make_server();` Pass cert/key to `listen(...)`.
- TLS operations (QB-98): `[[nodiscard]] bool set_tls_context(qb::io::ssl::Context)` and `[[nodiscard]] bool reload_certificates(std::filesystem::path cert, std::filesystem::path key)` (`1.1/http.h:1214,1228`). Present only for a secure transport with `QB_HAS_SSL`. The setter pins `http/1.1` ALPN and replaces the listener context; invalid input returns false without changing the serving context. Accepted sockets, including those awaiting their handshake, retain the old context. Call on the owner thread with a **fresh unpublished context**: copies share `SSL_CTX`, and pinning ALPN mutates that shared object. SNI callbacks are retained; contexts they select must already carry the same protocol ALPN. Certificate reload builds `Context::server(cert,key)` with defaults; it replaces custom mTLS/ciphers/callbacks/session-cache configuration. Neither operation promises session resumption across rotation.
- `template<typename TLSContext> requires std::same_as<std::remove_cvref_t<TLSContext>, qb::io::ssl::Context> [[nodiscard]] bool listen(qb::io::uri, TLSContext&&)` and `listen_no_start(qb::io::uri, TLSContext&&)` install that context before binding (`1.1/http.h:1238,1249`); the former starts accepting, the latter waits for `start()`. Both also require a secure transport. Exact-type deduction keeps historical path calls such as `listen(uri,{})` unambiguous; use a typed `Context`, not bare braces, for the new overload.
- Accepted roles are TLS server and generic methods, including fresh `Context::adopt`/`Context::share` wrappers. Client-only and DTLS contexts are refused before publication. The setter checks context usability and role and pins server ALPN; it does **not** prove every handshake prerequisite or require a static certificate (SNI/custom authentication may provide identity). The caller owns that policy (`src/qbm/http/detail/server_tls.cpp:11`).
- `listen` cert/key are `std::filesystem::path` (here and on the http2/http3/dual-stack `listen` overloads). Secure listen builds the `SSL_CTX` via `qb::io::ssl::create_server_context`, which resolves a **relative** cert/key path through `qb::io::sys::resolve_resource` (cwd first, then the executable's own directory); absolute paths are used unchanged. So `listen(uri, "cert.pem", "key.pem")` finds certs shipped next to the binary from any working directory. (String literals convert implicitly to `std::filesystem::path`.)
- `template<typename Derived> struct use { ... };` — type-builder mapping a Derived type to internal session/io_handler/server (tcp; `ssl::*` mirror for stcp/saccept).

### One-shot async client — `src/qbm/http/1.1/http.h`
- Non-upgrade 1xx responses are discarded; the callback/awaiter receives only the final response or terminal error. They do not cancel the timeout. Status 101 keeps the existing upgrade handling. Bodies are sent immediately even with `Expect: 100-continue`.
- `struct qb::http::async::Reply { Request request; Response response; }` — result pairing.
- `template<typename Func> using async::HTTP = session<Func, qb::io::transport::tcp>;` and `async::HTTPS = session<Func, qb::io::transport::stcp>` (**HTTPS needs `QB_HAS_SSL`**).
- Callback form: `template<typename Func> REQUEST(Request, Func&&, qb::duration timeout=qb::duration::zero(), bool verify_peer=true)` (method taken from request); verb helpers `GET/POST/PUT/DEL/HEAD/OPTIONS/PATCH(Request, Func&&, timeout, verify_peer)` force the method. `Func` is invoked with `async::Reply&&`. Sets Host/User-Agent/Accept-Encoding if absent.
- Coroutine form: `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<async::Reply> REQUEST(Request, qb::duration timeout=qb::duration::zero(), bool verify_peer=true)` and `GET/POST/PUT/DEL/HEAD/OPTIONS/PATCH(...)` — `co_await` yields `async::Reply`.
- `std::string host_header_value(const qb::io::uri&)` — Host header value: `origin::authority(uri)` (brackets IPv6 without its zone identifier, omits the scheme's default port).
- `template<typename Awaitable> auto run_sync(Awaitable&&)` — `src/qbm/http/coro.h:287` — drive any qbm-http awaitable to completion on the current I/O thread; a thin re-export of `qb::io::async::run_sync` so callers need not reach into `qb::io`. This is the **non-ws** `qb::http::run_sync`; `qb::http::ws::run_sync` (`src/qbm/http/ws/coro.h:505`) is the WebSocket-side alias of the same primitive. Use it from `main()`/tests, never from inside a coroutine already being driven.
  Usage: `auto reply = qb::http::run_sync(qb::http::GET(qb::http::Request{{"http://localhost:8080/"}}));`
- **`qb::duration::zero()` means "no timeout"**, not an immediate timeout.
Usage (coro): `auto reply = co_await qb::http::GET(qb::http::Request{qb::http::method::GET, qb::io::uri{"https://h/x"}});`

### Opt-in one-shot redirects — explicit `<qbm/http/redirect.h>`

`struct qb::http::RedirectOptions { std::size_t max_hops = 5; bool allow_cross_origin = false; };`
`struct qb::http::async::RedirectReply : Reply { std::vector<Reply> hops; };`
The existing `Reply` is unchanged. These overloads have required timeout, verification and options arguments. Callback storage is decayed by value and invoked as an lvalue with `async::RedirectReply&&`:

```cpp
namespace qb::http {
template <typename Completion>
requires std::is_invocable_v<std::decay_t<Completion>&, async::RedirectReply&&>
void REQUEST(Request request, Completion&& complete, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
template <typename Completion>
requires std::is_invocable_v<std::decay_t<Completion>&, async::RedirectReply&&>
void GET(Request request, Completion&& complete, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
template <typename Completion>
requires std::is_invocable_v<std::decay_t<Completion>&, async::RedirectReply&&>
void POST(Request request, Completion&& complete, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
template <typename Completion>
requires std::is_invocable_v<std::decay_t<Completion>&, async::RedirectReply&&>
void PUT(Request request, Completion&& complete, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
template <typename Completion>
requires std::is_invocable_v<std::decay_t<Completion>&, async::RedirectReply&&>
void DEL(Request request, Completion&& complete, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
template <typename Completion>
requires std::is_invocable_v<std::decay_t<Completion>&, async::RedirectReply&&>
void HEAD(Request request, Completion&& complete, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
template <typename Completion>
requires std::is_invocable_v<std::decay_t<Completion>&, async::RedirectReply&&>
void OPTIONS(Request request, Completion&& complete, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
template <typename Completion>
requires std::is_invocable_v<std::decay_t<Completion>&, async::RedirectReply&&>
void PATCH(Request request, Completion&& complete, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
}
```

Coroutine declarations use a deduced awaiter type; `co_await` yields `async::RedirectReply`:

```cpp
namespace qb::http {
[[nodiscard]] auto REQUEST(Request request, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
[[nodiscard]] auto GET(Request request, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
[[nodiscard]] auto POST(Request request, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
[[nodiscard]] auto PUT(Request request, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
[[nodiscard]] auto DEL(Request request, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
[[nodiscard]] auto HEAD(Request request, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
[[nodiscard]] auto OPTIONS(Request request, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
[[nodiscard]] auto PATCH(Request request, qb::duration timeout, bool verify_peer, RedirectOptions options);
}
```

`REQUEST` keeps the supplied method; the seven verbs set it. The default cap is five followed hops (zero follows none), with the terminal reply kept apart from `hops`; reaching the cap returns the received 3xx, never a generated 508. Request snapshots have ordinary preparation/compression state; replay uses the logical body, not a prepared snapshot. Complete bodies remain in history, which grows on actual followed hops without reserving `max_hops` entries. The timeout is per attempt. Final completion is deferred beyond session dispatch; destroying the coroutine awaiter suppresses later attempts, without cancelling an already-started session. Listener teardown drops queued callbacks. Before any reply, setup exceptions can propagate; a later-hop setup exception returns the preceding completed reply. Enqueue allocation failure is not recovered at the noexcept callback boundary.

Cross-origin following requires `allow_cross_origin=true`, then Authorization/Proxy-Authorization/Cookie/Origin/Referer and the cookie jar are cleared. HTTPS→HTTP is refused regardless. 301/302 change POST to GET and discard content; 303 discards content and uses GET unless HEAD; 307/308 preserve method/logical body. Missing/multiple Location values or next-attempt preparation refusal return the last completed reply. _(src/qbm/http/redirect.h:25-38; src/qbm/http/detail/redirect.cpp:233-270)_

Followed targets require strict absolute HTTP(S) resolution. Userinfo, malformed escapes/bytes, scoped IPv6 and IPvFuture are refused. Relative references retain raw escaped octets, slash segments and explicit empty queries; HTTP fragment inheritance applies. _(src/qbm/http/origin.h:106-192; src/qbm/http/detail/redirect.cpp:64-112,123-151,161-229)_

The chain owns each flight during startup, then preserves the existing session disposal contract. The terminal reply and history move into final delivery after dispatch; abandonment prevents subsequent flights. These are the startup, processing and helper entry points. _(src/qbm/http/redirect.h:92-162,174-200,215-340)_

Deferred delivery and queue teardown follow the existing listener contract. _(qb/src/qb/io/async/listener.h:622-675,866-888,1189-1201)_

### Persistent client — `qb::http1::Client` (alias `client`) — `src/qbm/http/1.1/client.h`
- Non-upgrade 1xx responses do not complete or advance the active request, enter statistics, or disable its timeout. Only final fields reach the callback/awaiter; status 101 retains the existing handling. No wait-for-100 upload handshake.
`class Client : public std::enable_shared_from_this<Client>` — same-origin keep-alive client; **non-copyable, must live in a `shared_ptr`**.
- `explicit Client(const std::string& base_uri); explicit Client(const qb::io::uri&);` — throws `std::invalid_argument` on non-http(s) scheme / missing host (http-only when `QB_HAS_SSL` off).
- `bool connect(ConnectionCallback);` and `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<ConnectResult> connect();` — `ConnectionCallback = void(bool connected, const std::string& error)`. During retirement it accepts the next intent but starts it after old callback/protocol dispatch unwinds; `is_connecting()` may be true before connected. Work may queue behind explicit intent with automatic reconnect disabled.
- `void disconnect();` — marks down before old notifications, fails the detached active + pending cohort with SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, and reports the old connect callbacks cancelled once. Reentrant requests/connects belong to the next cycle. Destruction abandons pending connect callbacks instead of notifying them. (`src/qbm/http/1.1/client.cpp:240-244,280-315,346-357,573-638`.)
- `bool push_request(Request, ResponseCallback);` and `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<Response> push_request(Request);` — `ResponseCallback=void(Response)`; callback form returns false if callback null or pending limit reached.
- `bool push_requests(std::vector<Request>, BatchResponseCallback);` and `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<std::vector<Response>> push_requests(std::vector<Request>);` — `BatchResponseCallback=void(std::vector<Response>)`, responses index-aligned.
- `void set_connect_timeout(qb::duration) noexcept` (default 30s); `set_request_timeout(qb::duration)` (default 60s); `set_auto_reconnect(bool)`; `set_max_pending_requests(...)` (default 1024); `void set_verify_peer(bool) noexcept` (default true, before connect) + `bool verify_peer() const noexcept`.
- `std::tuple<uint64_t,uint64_t,uint64_t> get_stats() const noexcept` = {total, successful, failed}; `bool is_connected()/is_connecting() const noexcept`; `get_active_request_count()`; `get_base_uri()`.
- `struct ConnectResult { bool ok{false}; std::string error_message; explicit operator bool() const noexcept; }`; aliases `ResponseCallback/BatchResponseCallback/ConnectionCallback`.
- `std::shared_ptr<Client> qb::http1::make_client(const std::string& base_uri);` / `make_client(const qb::io::uri&);` — required ownership form.
Usage: `auto c = qb::http1::make_client("https://h"); co_await c->connect(); auto resp = co_await c->push_request(req);`

### HTTP/1.1 protocol/parser — `1.1/protocol/*`
- `template<typename MessageType> struct Parser : public http_t` (`1.1/protocol/base.h:173`) — llhttp incremental parser; `parse(buffer,size)->http_errno_t`, `reset()`, `resume()`, `get_parsed_message()`, `headers_completed()`. Copyable and movable at every phase: it holds no pointer to itself, its callbacks find it through the state llhttp executes (QB-510). The parser fills the raw header map only; the message's typed `content_type()` derives from it on first read, on every framing path (QB-506).
- `template<typename IO_Handler,typename Trait> class base` (`base.h`) — `AProtocol`; `getMessageSize()` does Content-Length + chunked framing.
- `template<typename IO_Handler> class server` (`server.h`) / `client` (`client.h`) — parse Cookie / Set-Cookie (exceptions contained) and dispatch via `_io.on(...)`.
- `template<typename IO_Handler> using qb::http::protocol = ...` — selects server vs client by `IO_Handler::has_server`.

---

# Namespace `qb::http2` — HTTP/2 (`2/`) · **needs `QB_HAS_SSL`**

### Constants — `src/qbm/http/2/http2.h`
`namespace constants`: `DEFAULT_SESSION_TIMEOUT = std::chrono::seconds(60)` (qb::duration), `DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS = 50`, `STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT = std::chrono::seconds(30)`, `STREAM_INCOMPLETE_TIMEOUT = std::chrono::seconds(10)`, `CLEANUP_INTERVAL = std::chrono::seconds(5)` (all `qb::duration`).

### Server
- `class DefaultSession : public qb::http2::use<DefaultSession>::session<Server<DefaultSession>>` (`http2.h:1004`).
- `template<typename SessionType=DefaultSession> class Server : public internal::server<Server<SessionType>,SessionType>` — `Router& router()` (`http2.h:1031`).
- `template<typename Session=DefaultSession> std::unique_ptr<Server<Session>> make_server();` (`http2.h:1071`).
- `internal::server::drain(qb::duration deadline, std::function<void(qb::http::drain_outcome)> on_drained = {}) -> bool` (`http2.h:808`; Huly QB-91) -- the HTTP/1.1 server's contract: one report on the server's loop, `drained` when no HTTP session is left or `deadline`; false, and no change, when a drain is under way; `draining() const noexcept` (`http2.h:833`). The listener closes; each HTTP/2 connection shuts down in the two phases of RFC 9113 §6.8 -- `ServerHttp2Protocol::begin_graceful_shutdown()` (`2/protocol/server.h:270`) sends a GOAWAY naming 2^31-1 and a PING, and the PING's ACK runs `complete_graceful_shutdown()` (`2/protocol/server.h:296`): the final GOAWAY names the last stream the client opened, a stream above it is refused (`REFUSED_STREAM`), the connection closes after its last stream. A connection whose TLS handshake ends during the drain is sent only that final GOAWAY, naming stream 0, from `on(handshake)` (`http2.h:418-434`); an HTTP/1.1 session of the ALPN fallback that received nothing closes, one at work closes after its answer (`http2_begin_drain`, `http2.h:348`). At the deadline `http2_abort_drain` (`http2.h:376`) sends the final GOAWAY to a connection that never answered the PING and closes it once that is delivered, within qb-io's linger bound (aborted when `set_linger()` is zero or less); any other session is aborted. `graceful_shutdown_notice_pending()` (`2/protocol/server.h:314`) tells a connection that waits for the ACK.
- `internal::server::listen(qb::io::uri, std::filesystem::path cert, std::filesystem::path key) -> bool` — ALPN `{h2, http/1.1}`; binds **and** starts accepting, like the qb-io acceptor it derives from (`http2.h:900`). `listen_no_start(...)` is the bind-only opt-out (`http2.h:917`).
- `[[nodiscard]] bool set_tls_context(qb::io::ssl::Context)`; `[[nodiscard]] bool reload_certificates(std::filesystem::path cert, std::filesystem::path key)`; exact-`Context` forwarding overloads `listen(uri, context)` / `listen_no_start(uri, context)` (`2/http2.h:939,950,958,969`). Same publication, ownership, failure and complete-replacement contracts as HTTPS above, pinning server preference `h2` then `http/1.1`. Prepare each SNI-selected child with this list before publication. These operations cover HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 only; no corresponding HTTP/3 or dual-stack rotation operation is added.
- `internal::session`: `[[nodiscard]] bool reset_stream(uint32_t stream_id, ErrorCode=CANCEL, const std::string& reason={})`; `auto& operator<<(qb::http::Response&)` (validates stream_id>0 + status 100..599); `Router& router()`.
- `internal::io_handler::set_request_limits(qb::http::request_limits const&) noexcept` / `request_limits() const noexcept` (`http2.h:672`, `:680`) — the request limits of both protocols the server speaks, read live (`internal::session::http_request_limits()`, `http2.h:316`; Huly QB-94): an HTTP/2 request over one is answered on its stream -- `414` for `:path`, `431` for a field name, a field value or the field count of its header or trailer section (once the block is known well-formed: a malformed field stays a stream error -- a `content-length` too, judged over the limits or not, as is a length the block that ends the stream contradicts, Huly QB-1197), `413` for a declared `content-length` once the header block is valid or for DATA past the body limit (DATA past `content-length` is a stream error first) -- then `RST_STREAM(NO_ERROR)` (RFC 9113 §8.1), the connection going on. Until 3.3 the body was reset `ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM` against the HTTP/1.1 constant and the fields had no limit but the 1 MiB HPACK list, which stays (Huly QB-168, QB-94). `set_max_body_size(std::size_t) noexcept` / `max_body_size() const noexcept` (`http2.h:693`, `:701`) set and read the body limit alone. An HTTP/1.1 request of the ALPN fallback gets the HTTP/1.1 answers (`internal::session::http1_refuse_request`, `http2.h:398`).
- `template<typename Derived> struct use { ... session/io_handler/server ... }` (`http2.h:980-990`).
Usage: `auto s = qb::http2::make_server(); s->router().get("/", h); s->router().compile(); s->listen(uri,"cert.pem","key.pem");`

Stock session lifecycle: write progress and full-drain EOS collect logically completed contexts whose native stream is closed. Selection uses batches of 32 IDs (128 bytes of stack ID scratch, no heap scratch); each ID is refound and rechecked. One context leaves the registry before `POST_RESPONSE_SEND` and is released before the next candidate. The last owner triggers `REQUEST_COMPLETE` and member destruction; external owners may delay them. Same-drain rescans catch silent eligibility changes, including destruction with no hooks registered, while actual removals consume a budget fixed to the initial registry size. Selection is unordered, without a public stream-ID ordering guarantee. Reentry, active-protocol, connection and output-size guards apply before each scan/candidate; first-POST extraction cancels the remaining contexts. This changes no public API or Session data members and establishes no measured performance gain. Partial-write timing remains; EOS means framework output drain, not peer acknowledgment. Peer resets of unfinished routed streams, including `NO_ERROR`, cancel the stock context without a neutral public error event or a required new custom-I/O callback. (`src/qbm/http/2/http2.h:125-193,501-545`; `src/qbm/http/2/protocol/server.h:856-877`.)

### `qb::http2::Client` (alias `client`) — `src/qbm/http/2/client.h:163`
- Any number of informational 1xx HEADERS blocks may precede the final response, including CONTINUATION-split blocks. They preserve HPACK state and never appear in the final result or invoke the request callback. A 1xx with END_STREAM, status 101, or DATA before final headers resets the stream with PROTOCOL_ERROR; request timeouts and cancellation remain active.
- A locally reset stream is removed before its error notification. Reentrant cancellation of that stream cannot notify it again; a callback may submit the next request.
`class Client : public std::enable_shared_from_this<Client>, public qb::io::async::tcp::client<Client,qb::io::transport::stcp>, public qb::io::use<Client>::timeout` — TLS+ALPN-h2 only; **non-copyable, non-movable**; via `make_client`/`shared_ptr`.
- `explicit Client(const std::string& base_uri); explicit Client(const qb::io::uri&);`
- `bool connect(ConnectionCallback)` (pass `nullptr` for fire-and-forget; no default arg) / `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<ConnectResult> connect();`
- `void disconnect(); bool is_connected()/is_connecting() const noexcept` (connected = TCP + h2 handshake). `disconnect()` fails the outstanding work at once (`503`), sends `GOAWAY(NO_ERROR)` after what the connection still had to send, then qb-io shuts the sending side down (the server reads the GOAWAY, then EOF, no reset; the descriptor is released on the next connection or destruction) — at the latest after `static constexpr qb::duration Client::GOAWAY_FLUSH_LIMIT` (1 s) when the server stopped reading (`src/qbm/http/2/client.cpp:154-214`, `src/qbm/http/2/client.cpp:1108-1118`).
- `bool push_request(Request, ResponseCallback)` / `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<Response> push_request(Request)` (lazy connect). Past the pending cap `push_request` **rejects with `503 Service Unavailable`**; `push_requests` admits member by member, a member past the cap getting `503` at its index (callback still once, in order; returns `false` then) (DoS guard, matches http1/http3; `src/qbm/http/2/client.cpp:357-368`).
- `bool push_requests(std::vector<Request>, BatchResponseCallback)` / `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<std::vector<Response>> push_requests(std::vector<Request>)` (separate streams, request order).
- A completed batch leaves the client's batch registry before its callback runs; that callback may call `disconnect()` or enqueue another batch (`src/qbm/http/2/client.cpp:389-401`).
- A batch the client fails before every member is answered (explicit `disconnect()`, connection loss, exhausted reconnection run) still gets ONE callback: the responses already received are kept as received (an empty `200` stays a `200`, an admission-refused member keeps its `400`) and every unanswered member gets `503` with the failure reason as body (`src/qbm/http/2/client.cpp:332-339`).
- While sending queued requests, the client retains itself and rechecks its connection and h2 protocol before each send. A failed-send callback may disconnect or enqueue new work without sending the next request on a retired connection (`src/qbm/http/2/client.cpp:479-525`).
- Client stream identifiers are 31-bit (RFC 9113 §5.1.1): once a connection has opened stream 2^31-1, `ClientHttp2Protocol::stream_ids_exhausted()` is true and its `send_request` refuses; the client drains that connection like a graceful GOAWAY (active requests finish on it) and sends the pending ones on a new connection, or fails them with `503` when automatic reconnection is off (`src/qbm/http/2/client.cpp:491-499`, `src/qbm/http/2/protocol/client.h:1276-1287`).
- `void set_connect_timeout(qb::duration)` (default 30s); `set_request_timeout(qb::duration)` (default 60s); `void set_max_concurrent_streams(size_t)` (default 100); `void set_max_pending_requests(size_t) noexcept` (default 1024; bound on outstanding pending+active requests, 503 over-limit); `set_auto_reconnect(bool)` (default true; keeps the policy); `void set_verify_peer(bool) noexcept` (default true) + `bool verify_peer() const noexcept`.
- Reconnection run (`src/qbm/http/2/client.h:472-497`): `void enable_auto_reconnect(RetryPolicy policy = RetryPolicy{}) noexcept` / `void disable_auto_reconnect() noexcept` (the redis names; a scheduled attempt still fires); `[[nodiscard]] bool is_reconnecting() const noexcept` (an attempt scheduled or in flight); `[[nodiscard]] int reconnect_attempts() const noexcept` (attempts in the current run: reset by a connection that comes up, an explicit `connect()`, an explicit `disconnect()` — which starts no run, as on http1: a push after it connects on its own). `qb::http2::RetryPolicy` is `qb::http::RetryPolicy` (`src/qbm/http/2/client.h:93`). Attempt 1 immediate, then the policy's waits; exhausted -> the waiting requests get `503` with body `Reconnection attempts exhausted (N)` and the client stays down until the next `connect()` (explicit, or a later push's auto-connect). Every attempt fires from the client's timer, never from inside the failing handler; a push made from a failure callback queues behind the scheduled attempt.
- `std::tuple<uint64_t,uint64_t,uint64_t> get_stats() const noexcept`; `get_active_request_count()`; `get_base_uri()`.
- `struct ConnectResult { bool ok{false}; std::string error_message; explicit operator bool() const noexcept; }`; aliases `ResponseCallback/BatchResponseCallback/ConnectionCallback`.
- `std::shared_ptr<Client> qb::http2::make_client(const std::string&);` / `make_client(const qb::io::uri&);`
Usage: `auto c = qb::http2::make_client("https://h"); auto resp = co_await c->push_request(req);`

### `qb::http::RetryPolicy` — `src/qbm/http/retry_policy.h:25`
`using RetryPolicy = qb::io::reconnect_policy;` — qb-io's shared reconnection backoff (`<qb/io/reconnect.h>`, `qb/src/qb/io/reconnect.h:218`), the same type as `qb::redis::RetryPolicy`; the HTTP/2 client's run follows it. **All time fields are `qb::duration`.**

```cpp
struct qb::io::reconnect_policy {
  int           max_attempts    = -1;      // per run, -1 = unlimited
  qb::duration  initial_delay   = 100ms;   // the wait before attempt 2
  qb::duration  max_delay       = 30s;     // the wait never grows past this
  double        multiplier      = 2.0;     // below 1 reads as 1
  bool          jitter          = true;    // +-25 % on every wait
  qb::duration  connect_timeout = {};      // per attempt; zero = the client's own (the h2 client keeps set_connect_timeout())
  std::function<void(int attempt, qb::duration next_delay)> on_retry;  // before each wait: attempts failed so far
};
```
Fluent setters (each returns `reconnect_policy&`): `with_max_attempts(int)`, `with_initial_delay(qb::duration)`, `with_max_delay(qb::duration)`, `with_multiplier(double)`, `with_jitter(bool)`, `with_connect_timeout(qb::duration)`, `with_on_retry(std::function<void(int,qb::duration)>)`. Pure: `[[nodiscard]] qb::duration next_delay(int attempt, std::mt19937 *rng = nullptr) const` — the wait after `attempt` failed attempts: 0 for `attempt < 1`, `initial_delay * multiplier^(attempt-1)` capped at `max_delay` (integer milliseconds), jittered when `rng` is given and `jitter` is on, never below 1 ms once positive; a zero wait stays zero. `[[nodiscard]] constexpr bool allows_attempt(int attempts) const noexcept` — whether a run that made `attempts` attempts may make another.

### HPACK (RFC 7541) — `src/qbm/http/2/protocol/hpack.h`
- `class Encoder { bool encode(const std::vector<HeaderField>&, std::vector<uint8_t>&); void set_peer_max_dynamic_table_size(uint32_t); void set_max_capacity(uint32_t); void reset(); }` — value-owned. `encode` validates every field first: on `false` nothing is appended and the table is untouched. The table holds min(`set_max_capacity`, peer limit); a size change is announced by a Dynamic Table Size Update at the start of the next block (the smallest size reached first, RFC 7541 §4.2). A field marked `sensitive` stays a never-indexed literal even on an exact table match; default-sensitive names and pseudo headers are never indexed. Value octets 0x80–0xFF are valid.
- `class Decoder { bool decode(const std::vector<uint8_t>&, std::vector<HeaderField>&, bool& out_is_possibly_incomplete); void set_max_dynamic_table_size(uint32_t); void set_max_header_list_size(uint32_t); void reset(); }` — false on protocol errors.
- `class DynamicTable { struct AddResult{bool added; std::size_t evicted;}; AddResult add(string,string); std::size_t set_max_byte_size(std::size_t); operator[](size_t); }` — ring buffer, newest-first, non-copyable/movable.
- `struct HeaderField { std::string name,value; bool sensitive=false; std::size_t hpack_size() const; bool is_pseudo_header() const; bool is_sensitive_by_default() const noexcept; }`.
- `namespace static_table`: `find_name_match(string_view)`, `find_exact_match(string_view,string_view)`, `get_entry(size_t)`, `is_valid_index(size_t)`; `constexpr std::array<...,61> STATIC_TABLE`.
- `enum class HpackError{SUCCESS,INVALID_INDEX,INTEGER_OVERFLOW,INSUFFICIENT_DATA,INVALID_INSTRUCTION,TABLE_SIZE_EXCEEDED,HEADER_LIST_SIZE_EXCEEDED,HUFFMAN_DECODE_ERROR,UNKNOWN_ERROR}`; `enum class InstructionType:uint8_t{...}`.
- `namespace convenience`: `encode_headers(vector<HeaderField>) -> vector<uint8_t>` (throws `std::invalid_argument` on an invalid field, never a partial block); `decode_headers(vector<uint8_t>) -> std::optional<vector<HeaderField>>`; `make_header(string,string) -> HeaderField`.

### Streams + frame handlers — `src/qbm/http/2/protocol/stream.h`, `src/qbm/http/2/protocol/server.h`
- `enum class Http2StreamConcreteState{IDLE,OPEN,RESERVED_LOCAL,RESERVED_REMOTE,HALF_CLOSED_LOCAL,HALF_CLOSED_REMOTE,CLOSED}`.
- `class Http2StreamBase { uint32_t id; Http2StreamConcreteState state; int64_t local_window_size,peer_window_size; bool is_closed()/can_send_data()/can_receive_data(); void transition_state(bool,bool); void mark_reset(ErrorCode,bool); }`; `struct Http2ClientStream : Http2StreamBase {...}`; `struct Http2ServerStream : Http2StreamBase {...}`.
- `class FlowControlManager { static int64_t update_window_safe(int64_t,uint32_t,int64_t) /*-1 on overflow*/; static bool should_send_window_update(uint32_t,uint32_t); static uint32_t calculate_window_threshold(int64_t,int divisor=2); }`.
- `template<typename StreamType> class StreamManager { struct CleanupCriteria{ qb::duration max_idle_time, max_age; bool cleanup_closed_streams, cleanup_reset_streams; uint32_t max_total_streams; }; std::size_t cleanup_streams(const CleanupCriteria&); StreamStats get_statistics() const; }` — **timeouts are `qb::duration`** (0 = no limit).
- events: `struct Http2StreamErrorEvent{uint32_t stream_id; ErrorCode; std::string message;}`, `Http2GoAwayEvent{ErrorCode; uint32_t last_stream_id; std::string debug_data;}`, `Http2PushPromiseEvent{uint32_t associated/promised_stream_id; qb::http::Headers headers;}`, `Http2ConnectionErrorEvent{ErrorCode; std::string message; bool fatal;}`.
- `template<typename IO_Handler> class ServerHttp2Protocol` (`src/qbm/http/2/protocol/server.h:78`) — non-copyable/non-movable:
  - `bool send_response(uint32_t stream_id, const qb::http::Response&)` — a response to `HEAD` ends the stream on its HEADERS (no DATA, `content-length` kept); the fields named by the response's `trailer` header, then its `trailers()`, leave in the trailer block after the body -- an empty body included -- not in the leading HEADERS, which gain a `trailer` announcement when the response has none — the request side follows the same rule, `ClientHttp2Protocol::send_request` sending them as soon as the body is out (`src/qbm/http/2/protocol/base.h:410-468`, Huly QB-1073); a forbidden field of `trailers()` refuses the response (stream error) or the request (`false`) before anything is sent. A received trailer section is checked against the one trailer list on both sides and lands in `trailers()` (and the headers, for 3.x); the client completes a response whose trailer section was not announced (a second header block that ends the stream). A request announcing fields it does not set waits for `send_request_trailers()` on the protocol (`set_explicit_request_trailers(true)`, the default); `qb::http2::Client` sets it false, so such a stream ends after the body with an empty trailer block (`src/qbm/http/2/protocol/client.h:1289-1306`);
  - `[[nodiscard]] std::optional<PushPromiseFailureReason> send_push_promise(uint32_t associated, uint32_t promised /*even, non-zero*/, qb::http::Request pseudo_headers)` (needs peer `SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH=1`); the promised request is a `GET` or a `HEAD` without content or trailer section (RFC 9113 §8.4; else `INVALID_PROMISED_REQUEST`) on a stream the client opened (else `INVALID_ASSOCIATED_STREAM`), its id above every one promised before and at most 2^31-1 (else `INVALID_PROMISED_STREAM`), none once a GOAWAY was sent or received (`CONNECTION_INACTIVE`); its fields are sent as a client's request sends them (`append_sent_request_fields`, `src/qbm/http/2/protocol/base.h:396`: `HeaderValidator::is_sent_request_field`, `base.cpp:150`, less the fields its `connection` header names -- no connection-specific field, `te` only as `trailers`, no `host`, no `content-length`; Huly QB-1191); on success answer the reserved stream with `send_response(promised, response)`;
  - `void send_rst_stream(uint32_t, ErrorCode, const std::string& msg="", bool close_context=true) noexcept`;
  - `uint32_t cleanup_idle_streams(qb::duration max_idle=std::chrono::seconds(30), qb::duration max_incomplete=std::chrono::seconds(10)) noexcept` — idle counts from the last progress the sweep observed (response HEADERS/DATA sent, stream WINDOW_UPDATE received); `max_incomplete` bounds the AGE of a stream whose request is incomplete;
  - `[[nodiscard]] bool is_stream_closed(uint32_t) const`; `static bool is_valid_header_field(const std::string& name, const std::string& value) noexcept`.
- `template<typename IO_Handler> using client_protocol/server_protocol = ClientHttp2Protocol/ServerHttp2Protocol<IO_Handler>` (`http2.h:73-77`).
- `bool qb::http::well_known::is_hop_by_hop(const std::string& header_name)` (`src/qbm/http/2/protocol/server.h:53`) — classifies hop-by-hop headers (forbidden in HTTP/2).

# Namespace `qb::http3` — HTTP/3 / QUIC (`3/`) · **needs `QBM_HTTP_HAS_HTTP3`**

### `qb::http3::Client` (alias `client`) — `src/qbm/http/3/client.h:110`
`class Client : public std::enable_shared_from_this<Client>, public qb::io::async::quic::endpoint` — persistent same-origin client; **heap-owned via `shared_ptr`**.
- `explicit Client(const std::string& base_uri); explicit Client(const qb::io::uri&);` — throws `std::invalid_argument` unless scheme is https.
- `bool connect(ConnectionCallback)` (ALPN `{"h3"}`) / `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<ConnectResult> connect();`
- `void disconnect(); [[nodiscard]] bool is_connected() const noexcept` (QUIC + h3 ready).
- From a callback inside a native HTTP/3 read, `disconnect()` marks the client logically down at once. Protocol teardown, QUIC close and failure of still-active requests wait until the read returns; GOAWAY may continue invoking other pending-request callbacks meanwhile. A reentrant `connect(callback)` fails without starting a handshake, new requests get an immediate `503`, and explicit disconnect does not auto-reconnect (`src/qbm/http/3/client.cpp:76-85,119-171,235-240,300-311,749-757,813-851`).
- During ordinary `disconnect()`, the client publishes the closed state before failure callbacks run and rejects their reentrant connect or request attempts until close finishes (`src/qbm/http/3/client.cpp:119-171`). Event callbacks retain the client through endpoint dispatch even if user code releases its last external `shared_ptr` (`src/qbm/http/3/client.cpp:20-36,773-787,813-817,854-872`).
- Failure to start the QUIC connection, a connect timeout or a remote close retires the old transport before failure callbacks can start another attempt. Old requests are failed before connection callbacks can queue new work; the qb-io endpoint refreshes its internally owned native backend on retry (`src/qbm/http/3/client.cpp:93-115,500-542,623-640,783-810`; `qb/src/qb/io/async/quic/endpoint.h:99-136,489-518`).
- The connect timer captures its attempt's epoch and does nothing after a later attempt begins. Explicit `disconnect()` of an in-progress attempt reports failure to that attempt's connection callbacks once; their cancelled timer cannot fail the next attempt (`src/qbm/http/3/client.cpp:101-114,119-171,470-527,623-640`).
- The pending-request drain retains the client and rechecks connection, protocol and shutdown state before each submission, including after a failed submit invokes user code (`src/qbm/http/3/client.cpp:386-467`).
- If the transport closes synchronously during request submission, the request already removed from the pending queue receives a synthesized `503` instead of being installed in the active registry of the closed connection, even if an old failure callback throws; its saved exception propagates afterward. Connect success/failure notify their other callbacks before propagating a callback exception; explicit disconnect also completes transport cleanup (`src/qbm/http/3/client.cpp:119-171,386-467,470-527,545-595`).
- `bool push_request(Request, ResponseCallback)` (auto-connects; false if callback null or the pending cap refused the request, its 503 already delivered — as http1/http2) / `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<Response> push_request(Request)`.
- `[[nodiscard]] request_id push_request_with_id(Request, ResponseCallback)` (`request_id=std::uint64_t`; 0 on immediate failure); `bool cancel_request(request_id id, const std::string& reason="HTTP/3 request cancelled")` (resets active stream with H3 error 0x010c = `NGHTTP3_H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED`; false if id unknown). Active cancellation retains the client through its callback and stream reset even if the callback releases the last external owner (`src/qbm/http/3/client.cpp:276-287`).
- `bool push_requests(std::vector<Request>, BatchResponseCallback)` / `[[nodiscard]] async::awaiter<std::vector<Response>> push_requests(std::vector<Request>)` (index-aligned; empty input → `callback({})`). Members are admitted one by one exactly as `push_request` admits one: an invalid member gets its 400 and a member past `set_max_pending_requests` its 503, at its index, before any state exists for it; the callback runs once, at once when nothing was admitted; returns `false` when the cap refused a member, as http1/http2 (`src/qbm/http/3/client.cpp:330-340`).
- `void set_max_pending_requests(std::size_t) noexcept` (default 10000; queued + active bound, 503 past it); `void set_max_concurrent_streams(std::size_t) noexcept` (default 100); `void set_max_body_size(std::size_t) noexcept` (default 64 MiB, exceed resets stream); `void set_connect_timeout(qb::duration) noexcept` (default 30s, ≤0 disables); `void set_request_timeout(qb::duration) noexcept` (default 60s, ≤0 disables); `void set_auto_reconnect(bool) noexcept` (default true); `void set_verify_peer(bool) noexcept` (default true).
- The QUIC peer's `max_streams_bidi` is a concurrent stream quota, not a lifetime request count. Qb returns a slot on close for a client-initiated request stream delivered through `stream_open_cb`; ngtcp2 renews implicitly opened streams itself. Sequential requests can reuse one HTTP/3 connection beyond the initial quota (`qb/src/qb/io/quic.cpp:1122,1626-1653`; `qbm/http/tests/system/http3/http3-loopback.cpp:1361-1420`).
- `std::tuple<uint64_t,uint64_t,uint64_t> get_stats() const noexcept`; `get_active_request_count()`; `get_stream_state_count()` (streams the connection keeps state for; does not grow with the requests made); `max_http3_body_size()`; `get_base_uri()`.
- `struct ConnectResult { bool ok{false}; std::string error_message; explicit operator bool() const noexcept; }`; aliases `ResponseCallback/BatchResponseCallback/ConnectionCallback/request_id`.
- `std::shared_ptr<Client> qb::http3::make_client(const std::string&);` / `make_client(const qb::io::uri&);`
Usage: `auto c = qb::http3::make_client("https://h"); auto resp = co_await c->push_request(req);`

### Server — `src/qbm/http/3/http3.h`
- `class DefaultSession : public qb::http3::use<DefaultSession>::session<Server<DefaultSession>>` (`http3.h:1003`).
- `template<typename SessionType=DefaultSession> class Server : public internal::server<Server<SessionType>,SessionType>` (`http3.h:1016`); `template<typename Session=DefaultSession> std::unique_ptr<Server<Session>> make_server();` (`http3.h:1029`); alias `template<...> using server = Server<Session>`.
- `internal::server::listen(const qb::io::uri&, const std::filesystem::path& cert, const std::filesystem::path& key) -> bool` (ALPN `{"h3"}`; also a `std::string`-uri overload) (`http3.h:695`); `[[nodiscard]] Router& router() noexcept` (`http3.h:608`); `void set_request_limits(qb::http::request_limits const&) noexcept` / `request_limits() const noexcept` (`http3.h:633`, `:641`; Huly QB-94 -- defaults the `protocol_limits` constants, a 64 MiB body; a request over one is answered -- `414` for `:path`, `431` for a regular field's name or value or a section's field count once the section ends (once the request is known well-formed: a field over the limits is judged before it is dropped, a `content-length` that a stream ended by its header or trailer section contradicts refuses it -- Huly QB-1197), `413` for a declared `content-length` at the end of its header section or for its DATA -- then STOP_SENDING(H3_NO_ERROR), RFC 9114 §4.1.1 (`answer_refused_request`, `protocol/connection.h:749`); a reset -- a client's 502 -- until 3.3, Huly QB-168, QB-94; nghttp3 bounds a section before these: a QPACK name past 256 bytes, a section past the advertised 64 KiB, are connection errors); `void set_max_body_size(std::size_t) noexcept` (`http3.h:650`; the body limit alone, 0 = none); `http3_request_limits()` (`http3.h:666`) is the connection's hook.
- `void graceful_shutdown()` (`http3.h:731`) — two phases on every connection open now (RFC 9114 §5.2, Huly QB-91): notice GOAWAY with the largest stream id, then final GOAWAY with the first request not read, rejecting requests at or above that id (`H3_REQUEST_REJECTED`). Each peer waits two of its own smoothed RTTs, at least 1 ms; an older custom backend without a per-connection estimate uses aggregate RTT. One server timer services the separate due times (`shutdown_notice_wait`, `http3.h:351`; `arm_notice_timer`, `http3.h:366`; `send_final_goaways`, `http3.h:414`). A connection closes with `H3_NO_ERROR` only once its last request stream has closed and the peer has acknowledged the control stream carrying GOAWAY (`control_stream_acknowledged`, `protocol/connection.h:1468`). Returns at once; admission remains open and later connections are served.
- `drain(qb::duration deadline, std::function<void(qb::http::drain_outcome)> on_drained = {}) -> bool` (`http3.h:759`) — same two phases, bounded by the drain deadline, with native admission of new Initial packets disabled before another connection is allocated (QB-1098). A handshake already in progress, or accepted by a legacy backend without admission control, serves no request: final GOAWAY stream 0 precedes request dispatch, then the connection closes after GOAWAY acknowledgement (`dispatch(connected)`, `http3.h:487`). Reports once on the server's loop: `drained` at zero connections or `deadline` after sending final GOAWAY and closing those still open. False when already draining; `draining() const noexcept` (`http3.h:781`). UDP endpoint remains bound until `close()`.
- `[[nodiscard]] std::size_t http3_stream_state_count() const noexcept` (`http3.h:677`) — streams the HTTP/3 connections retain, following requests in flight rather than requests already served.
- `internal::session`: per-stream server session; `operator<<(Response&)` (HEAD-aware) (`http3.h:223`).
- Trailers and `:authority`, both sides: the adapter's `submit_response` / `submit_request` (`src/qbm/http/3/protocol/connection.h:1589`, `:1648`) build the trailer section with `detail::plan_trailers` (`:437`) and `make_trailer_block` (`:419`) before anything is submitted -- the fields the `trailer` header announces, then `trailers()`; an announced-but-unset field or an empty body still sends the message -- and a received trailer section lands in `trailers()` (and the headers, for 3.x), refused on the one trailer list (Huly QB-1073). `:authority` is `qb::http::origin::authority` (Huly QB-1064).
- `template<typename Derived> struct use { ... session/server ... }` (`http3.h:987`).

### Dual-stack (HTTP/2 + HTTP/3) — `src/qbm/http/3/dual_stack.h` · **namespace `qb::http`** (not `qb::http3`)
- `template<typename Http2Session=qb::http2::DefaultSession, typename Http3Session=qb::http3::DefaultSession> class qb::http::dual_stack_server` (`dual_stack.h:48`) — runs HTTP/2 (TCP+TLS) and HTTP/3 (QUIC) side by side; `router()` returns a `router_facade` registering each route on **both** tables.
- `class router_facade { add_route/get/post/put/del/patch/options/head(...); compile(); }`.
- `void set_request_limits(qb::http::request_limits const&) noexcept` (`dual_stack.h:287`) sets both stacks' (the HTTP/2 server's, which its HTTP/1.1 fallback reads, and the HTTP/3 server's -- its own 64 MiB body default giving way); `request_limits() const noexcept` (`dual_stack.h:297`) reads the HTTP/2 stack's; `set_max_body_size(std::size_t) noexcept` (`dual_stack.h:305`) sets both bodies alone (Huly QB-94).
- `bool drain(qb::duration deadline, std::function<void(qb::http::drain_outcome)> on_drained = {})` (`dual_stack.h:322`; Huly QB-91) drains both stacks with one deadline and reports once: `drained` when both drained, `deadline` when either met it; false, and no change, when either already drains; `draining() const noexcept` (`dual_stack.h:351`).
- `bool listen(qb::io::uri tcp_tls_uri, qb::io::uri quic_uri, const std::filesystem::path& cert, const std::filesystem::path& key)` (also a `std::string`-uri overload) — true only if both bind; **all-or-nothing** (rolls back the side that came up and returns false if the other fails) (`dual_stack.h:372-373`).
- Not copyable; `noexcept` move construction and assignment keep `router()` bound to the destination, and the moved-from server holds no stack (destroy or assign only). Move it before `listen()` (`src/qbm/http/3/dual_stack.h:227-253`).
- `template<...> std::unique_ptr<dual_stack_server<...>> qb::http::make_dual_stack_server();` (`dual_stack.h:447`).
Usage: `auto s = qb::http::make_dual_stack_server(); s->router().get("/", h); s->router().compile(); s->listen(tcp_uri, quic_uri, "cert.pem","key.pem");`

### nghttp3 connection adapter — `src/qbm/http/3/protocol/connection.h`
`template<typename Owner> class connection` (Owner supplies stream-I/O + event hooks via `requires`; non-copyable, move-constructible):
- `enum class role{client,server}`; `connection(Owner&, std::uint64_t connection_id, role)` — qpack_blocked_streams=32, max_field_section_size=64 KiB; throws `std::runtime_error` on nghttp3 failure.
- `bool bind_local_streams(); bool read_stream(std::uint64_t, std::string_view data, bool fin); void add_ack_offset(std::uint64_t, std::uint64_t bytes); bool submit_request(std::uint64_t, const qb::http::Request&); bool submit_response(std::uint64_t, const qb::http::Response&); bool submit_shutdown_notice(); bool shutdown(); [[nodiscard]] bool is_drained() const noexcept;`

# Namespace `qb::http::ws` — WebSocket (RFC 6455) (`ws/`) · **needs `QB_HAS_SSL`**

> WebSocket is part of qbm-http (not a separate module). Include `<qbm/http/http.h>` (pulls `src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h` under `QB_HAS_SSL`).

### Messages — `src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h`
- `enum opcode : unsigned char { Continuation=0, _Text=1, _Binary=2, _Close=8, _Ping=9, _Pong=10, Text=129, Binary=130, Close=136, Ping=137, Pong=138 }` — lowercase-prefixed are bare opcodes; capitalized are FIN-set composites.
- `bool is_utf8(std::string_view) noexcept` — RFC 3629 validator (gates Text payloads and close reasons).
- `struct Message { unsigned char fin_rsv_opcode=0; bool masked=false; qb::allocator::pipe<char> _data; pipe<char>& data() noexcept; std::size_t size() const noexcept; template<typename T> Message& operator<<(T const&); void reset(); }`.
- `struct MessageText : Message` (0x81; UTF-8 on wire); `struct MessageBinary : Message` (0x82); `struct MessagePing : Message` (peer must echo); `struct MessagePong : Message`.
- `enum class CloseStatus : std::uint16_t { Normal=1000, GoingAway=1001, ProtocolError=1002, DataNotAccepted=1003, ... MessageTooBig=1009, ... TLSHandshakeFailed=1015 }` — 1004/1005/1006/1015 reserved and rejected.
- `constexpr bool is_sendable_close_code(std::uint16_t) noexcept` — true iff in [1000..4999] and not 1004/1005/1006/1015.
- `struct MessageClose : Message { MessageClose()=delete; explicit MessageClose(CloseStatus=Normal, std::string_view reason="closed normally"); explicit MessageClose(std::uint16_t status, std::string_view reason); }` — throws `std::invalid_argument` on reserved/out-of-range code; truncates reason to 123 bytes on a UTF-8 boundary.
- `std::string generateKey()` — base64 of a random 16-byte nonce for `Sec-WebSocket-Key`.
- `struct qb::http::WebSocketRequest : http::Request { WebSocketRequest()=delete; explicit WebSocketRequest(const std::string& key); }` — pre-filled upgrade GET (no `Host`: set it when writing one by hand; a qbm-http server answers 400 without one, QB-1186).

### Protocol framer — `src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h`
- `template<typename IO_> class qb::protocol::ws_internal::base : public qb::io::async::AProtocol<IO_> { base()=delete; explicit base(IO_& io); void set_max_payload_size(size_t); [[nodiscard]] bool server_draining() const noexcept; std::size_t getMessageSize() noexcept final; void onMessage(std::size_t) noexcept final; void reset() noexcept final; using close=event_close; ping=event_ping; pong=event_pong; message=event_message; }` — shared RFC 6455 framer; masking direction, opcode/RSV/length-minimality/UTF-8 validation, fragment reassembly, auto Ping reply, auto Close echo. `set_max_payload_size(0)`=unlimited (default `protocol_limits::MAX_BODY_SIZE`; exceed → close `MessageTooBig`).
- `template<typename IO_> class qb::protocol::ws_server` — server handshake (validates GET + Upgrade/Connection + key + Version 13; emits 101 with `Sec-WebSocket-Accept`; rejects with 400 + `not_ok()`); `struct sending_http_response { qb::http::Response& response; }`.
- `template<typename IO_> class qb::protocol::ws_client` — client handshake validator (checks 101, tokens, `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` in constant time; `not_ok()` on mismatch).
- `template<typename IO_> using qb::http::ws::protocol = ...` — selects `ws_server` when `IO_::has_server` else `ws_client`.
- `server_draining()` (`src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h:655`) reports the server-initiated close. A custom Close observer must not echo when it is true. This does not transfer ownership of an extracted session back to its former HTTP server.
- In a retained in-place upgrade, `begin_server_drain` queues Close 1001 (`src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h:660-674`). During drain, `processDataFrame` suppresses application data dispatch (`src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h:583-585`); `processControlFrame` suppresses application Ping/Pong callbacks but still sends the required protocol Pong before the peer Close arrives; it preserves the peer Close callback while finishing queued output (`src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h:510-580`).

### CRTP client — `src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h`
`template<typename T, typename Transport=qb::io::transport::tcp> class WebSocket : public qb::io::async::tcp::client<WebSocket<T,Transport>,Transport>, public qb::io::use<WebSocket<T,Transport>>::timeout`
Drives TCP connect + HTTP upgrade + protocol switch; forwards `ping/pong/message/closed/disconnected/error/connected` events to parent `T::on(...)` if present.
- `void set_ping_interval(qb::duration interval=qb::duration::zero())` — auto-ping keepalive after a verified upgrade; **zero/negative disables**.
- `void connect(const qb::io::uri& remote, qb::duration timeout=qb::duration::zero(), bool verify_peer=true)` — connect to `ws://`/`wss://`, install protocol, send upgrade. A positive timeout is one deadline across transport and Upgrade; zero disables it. An active transport is retired before reconnect, and its input/output buffers are cleared before the next handshake. A retry from a failure callback starts after the old transport's disconnect dispatch; after the peer's EOF that transport is closed already (qb-io `dispose()`), so a `connect()` from the `disconnected` callback starts in the same loop pass. The client rejects an unoffered `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions` response before `connected`.
- `void disconnect(int reason=1)` / `void disconnect(qb::io::async::event::disconnect_reason reason)` — cancel an unfinished connection and its deadline, then close the transport while forwarding the reason to qb-io's `disconnected` event. The zero-argument call remains valid through the default. An in-flight connector callback is inert after cancellation or client destruction; stack and `unique_ptr` clients are supported.
- `connected`, parsed-handshake/protocol `error`, and `disconnected` user callbacks are delivered after parser/I/O dispatch and may release the client. A transport connect failure or explicit pending `disconnect()` may report `error` synchronously. A pre-101 transport close reports `error` once. The `sending_http_request` hook remains synchronous; after it returns, a cancelled, replaced, or destroyed attempt sends no Upgrade request. Frames pipelined with the 101 are delivered after `connected`, in wire order.
- `void close(CloseStatus=Normal, std::string_view reason="closed normally")` — queue a Close frame (no TCP teardown); throws `std::invalid_argument` on reserved code; call `disconnect()` after for immediate teardown.
- `void set_subprotocols(std::vector<std::string>)` / `void add_subprotocol(std::string)` — offer list; each must be a valid RFC 7230 token (else `std::invalid_argument`); before connect.
- `std::string_view negotiated_subprotocol() const noexcept` — selected subprotocol (valid after `connected`).
- `template<typename ToSend> WebSocket& operator<<(ToSend&& msg)` — queue outbound; Message-derived values forcibly masked (client frames MUST be masked); sending `MessageClose` sets `_close_sent`.
- `template<typename T> using WebSocketSecure = WebSocket<T, qb::io::transport::stcp>` — wss flavor.

### Callback client — `src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h`
`template<typename Transport=qb::io::transport::tcp> class Client : public WebSocket<Client<Transport>,Transport>` — chainable setters (each returns `Client&`): `on_connected/on_message/on_ping/on_pong/on_closed/on_error/on_disconnected/on_sending_http_request`.
Aliases: `using ClientSecure = Client<stcp>; using client = Client<tcp>; using client_secure = Client<stcp>`.
Usage: `qb::http::ws::client c; c.on_message([](auto&&){...}).on_connected([](auto&&){...}); c.connect(qb::io::uri{"ws://h/path"});`

### Coroutine API — `src/qbm/http/ws/coro.h`
- `struct ConnectResult { bool ok{false}; }`; `struct CloseResult { bool ok{true}; }`.
- `struct IncomingFrame { enum class Kind:std::uint8_t{Message,Ping,Pong,Close,Disconnected}; Kind kind{Disconnected}; std::string payload; bool is_text{false}; std::uint16_t close_code{0}; std::string close_reason; }` — owning value safe to store past the `co_await`.
- `template<typename Transport=qb::io::transport::tcp> class coro_client : public WebSocket<coro_client<Transport>,Transport>` — coroutine-first; non-copyable/non-movable:
  - `[[nodiscard]] auto connect(const qb::io::uri& remote, qb::duration timeout=qb::duration::zero());` and `connect(std::string_view remote_uri, qb::duration timeout=qb::duration::zero())` — yields `ConnectResult`.
  - `[[nodiscard]] auto receive()` — yields next `IncomingFrame` in order; resolves immediately with `Disconnected` once gone; throws `std::logic_error` if another live awaiter is parked (one consumer). Destruction of a suspended awaiter makes its reservation inactive; later delivery uses a successor or the existing buffer policy.
  - `[[nodiscard]] auto close_async(CloseStatus=Normal, std::string_view reason="closed normally")` — yields `CloseResult`; validates the Close frame before publishing coroutine state, so reserved code/invalid UTF-8 rejection leaves a later valid close available; `std::logic_error` if another live close waiter is pending. Abandoning a waiter does not retract queued frame bytes; no complete allocation/serialization rollback guarantee.
  - `void set_pending_cap(std::size_t) noexcept` (default 1024; full→drop oldest; 0 disables buffering). A lowered cap applies at once (a queue above it is trimmed to its newest frames); 0 never purges what is buffered (`src/qbm/http/ws/coro.h:267-286`).
  - `using coro_client_secure = coro_client<qb::io::transport::stcp>`.
- `template<typename Awaitable> auto run_sync(Awaitable&&)` — drive a WS awaitable to completion on the current I/O thread (thin alias over `qb::io::async::run_sync`).
- `template<typename Self, typename Server> class coro_session : public qb::io::use<Self>::tcp::template client<Server>` — CRTP base for a server-side WS session written as a coroutine (`Self` defines `task<void> run()`); keeps the session shared_ptr alive across suspensions:
  - `bool accept_upgrade(qb::http::Request&, qb::http::Response&)` — single router integration point: apply handshake hook, `switch_protocol<WS_Protocol>`, send response, spawn `run()`. Returns false (and disconnects) on refusal/invalid handshake. Must run on the transport's I/O thread.
  - `[[nodiscard]] auto next_frame()` — yields queued inbound `IncomingFrame` values first; after transport disconnection and an empty queue, resolves `Disconnected`; throws `std::logic_error` if a live awaiter is already parked. A destroyed suspended awaiter releases its reservation as on the client.
  - `[[nodiscard]] auto close_async(CloseStatus=Normal, std::string_view reason="closed normally")` — server-side close; throws as above. A close already sent, including a protocol-initiated server drain, is awaited without another Close frame. The peer Close remains an owning `IncomingFrame::Close` with its code/reason before disconnection; completion is scheduled through the coroutine scheduler (`src/qbm/http/ws/coro.h:837-864,925-952`). The private `server_drain_active()` query reads the current protocol’s drain state (`src/qbm/http/ws/coro.h:616-618`).
  - `using HandshakeHook = std::function<bool(Self&, qb::http::Request&, qb::http::Response&)>; void set_handshake_hook(HandshakeHook)` — pre-upgrade hook (negotiate subprotocol / add headers / return false to reject; a throwing hook is a rejection); before `accept_upgrade`. A refusal keeps a status ≥ 300 (redirect or error) and answers `400` for anything below, the default 200 included (`src/qbm/http/ws/coro.h:639-655`).
  - `void set_pending_cap(std::size_t) noexcept` (default 1024).
Usage (coro client): `qb::http::ws::coro_client ws; auto r = co_await ws.connect(qb::io::uri{"ws://h/p"}); auto f = co_await ws.receive();`

The `http_awaiter` returned by `receive()` / `next_frame()` / `close_async()` now has a lifetime-aware concrete deduced operation type. Keep `auto`/`co_await` at call sites and rebuild consumers sharing these template definitions consistently. Public ordinary HTTP `async::awaiter<T>` / `make_awaiter` keep their existing callback path; actor cancellation is unchanged. (`src/qbm/http/coro.h:182-218,232-259`; `src/qbm/http/ws/coro.h:431-484,895-915,925-953`.)

### WS pipe serialization — `src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h:2046`
`template<> pipe<char>& pipe<char>::put<Message>(const Message&);` (and `MessagePing/MessagePong/MessageText/MessageBinary/MessageClose/WebSocketRequest`) — frame onto the outbound pipe (masks when `msg.masked`); invoked indirectly via `operator<<`.

---

# Build / integration

- `find_package` / `qb_load_modules(...)`, link target `qbm::http`, include `<qbm/http/http.h>`.
- `http.h` pulls: `src/qbm/http/1.1/http.h` + `src/qbm/http/1.1/client.h` always; `src/qbm/http/2/http2.h` + `src/qbm/http/ws/ws.h` under `QB_HAS_SSL`; `src/qbm/http/3/http3.h` + `src/qbm/http/3/client.h` + `src/qbm/http/3/dual_stack.h` under `QBM_HTTP_HAS_HTTP3`. Both `src/qbm/http/1.1/http.h` and `src/qbm/http/1.1/client.h` include `coro.h` — which defines `async::http_awaiter` (`src/qbm/http/coro.h:162`), the `async::awaiter<T>` alias (`src/qbm/http/coro.h:232`), `async::make_awaiter` (`src/qbm/http/coro.h:247`) and `qb::http::run_sync` (`src/qbm/http/coro.h:287`) — so it always arrives with the umbrella header; you never include it directly. Middleware: include `src/qbm/http/middleware/all.h` (or individual headers / `src/qbm/http/middleware/make.h`).
- Reference qb-core / qb-io types (`qb::io::uri`, `qb::allocator::pipe<char>`, `qb::json`, `qb::duration`, `qb::wall_time`, `qb::icase_unordered_map`, `qb::unordered_map`, async client/awaiter, transports) in the qb framework Factbook — not restated here.
